maria_prod: Hey support — we've been seeing elevated API latency for token exchanges and occasional 401s from our prod key in us-west-2. First bad request id I captured: req_2024020201abc123, time ~2024-02-02T15:16:07Z. Can you advise quick repro steps?

alex_supp: Thanks @maria_prod — sorry you're hitting this. Can you attach a minimal curl that reproduces the 401/latency? If possible include the X-Request-ID header from your app logs and any SDK request ids. Also tell us whether this is Hosted or Dedicated.

maria_prod: Hosted. Here's a redacted curl we run from our backend (we strip auth when posting here):
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: req_2024020201abc123" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-6b","input":"hello"}'
```
Response was a 401 + 1.8s latency on a few hits, 200s on one. App logs show: `auth: token refresh ok` then `request failed: 401 unauthorized (req_2024020201abc123)`.

alex_supp: Ok. Can you run the minimal SDK repros (quick Python/JS/Go) so we can capture the SDK-level request id and trace? Paste outputs here. Use the header override so we preserve your request id.

alex_supp: Python snippet:
```
# python repro.py
import requests
h={"Authorization":"Bearer REDACTED","Content-Type":"application/json","X-Request-ID":"req_2024020201abc123"}
r=requests.post("https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate", json={"model":"gpt-6b","input":"hello"}, headers=h, timeout=10)
print(r.status_code, r.headers.get('X-Redwood-Req'), r.text[:200])
```

alex_supp: Node snippet:
```
// node repro.js
const fetch = require('node-fetch')
;(async()=>{
  const r = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate',{method:'POST',headers:{'Authorization':'Bearer REDACTED','Content-Type':'application/json','X-Request-ID':'req_2024020201abc123'}, body:JSON.stringify({model:'gpt-6b', input:'hello'})})
  console.log(r.status, r.headers.get('x-redwood-req'))
  console.log(await r.text())
})()
```

alex_supp: Go snippet:
```
// go run repro.go
package main
import (
  "bytes"; "fmt"; "net/http"; "io/ioutil"
)
func main(){
  body := bytes.NewBuffer([]byte(`{"model":"gpt-6b","input":"hello"}`))
  req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST","https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate", body)
  req.Header.Set("Authorization","Bearer REDACTED")
  req.Header.Set("X-Request-ID","req_2024020201abc123")
  client := &http.Client{}
  resp, err := client.Do(req)
  if err!=nil{fmt.Println("err",err);return}
  b,_ := ioutil.ReadAll(resp.Body)
  fmt.Println(resp.StatusCode, resp.Header.Get("X-Redwood-Req"), string(b)[:200])
}
```

maria_prod: Running the Python one now, will paste output.

diagnostic_bot: Diagnostic bundle request received — run the following to upload logs if you want Redwood support to pull traces automatically:
```
# capture debug bundle (Linux)
journalctl -u your-app -o short-iso --since "2024-02-02 15:00" > app.logs
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -F "file=@app.logs" https://diagnostics.redwood.ai/upload?token=DIAG_UPLOAD_TOKEN
```
(You can request a one-click upload token from support to avoid exposing logs publicly.)

jamie_sre: @alex_supp quick q — any signs of a throttling rule in us-west-2 or a broken KMS auth path? If it's Hosted, key rotation could cause ephemeral 401s. Also ask customer to check for skew between app clock and NTP — token validation is time-sensitive.

luis_devx: Also if you can, run a curl with curl's verbose flag to capture TLS handshake timings: `curl -v --trace-time --trace-ascii /tmp/trace.txt ...` and share the trace file. Helps root-cause slow TLS or renegotiation.

maria_prod: Python output: `401 None {"error":"unauthorized","message":"invalid token"}` — no X-Redwood-Req header returned. I uploaded app.logs to diagnostics (upload id diag_98765) and included the request id there.

alex_supp: Perfect, thanks. I'll escalate to infra with diag_98765 + req_2024020201abc123. For faster triage, can you also run the curl with `--resolve` from your environment to force us-west-2 endpoint and include `-w "\nTIME_TOTAL:%{time_total}\n"` so we capture total time? e.g.:
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: req_2024020201abc123" \
  --resolve api.redwood.ai:443:54.201.12.34 \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-6b","input":"hello"}' -w "\nTIME_TOTAL:%{time_total}\n"
```
(Replace IP with api endpoint IP you resolve from your VPC).

jamie_sre: I'll watch diag_98765 and correlate with our edge logs. If we see retries from the auth service, we'll post a quick update here.

maria_prod: Running the verbose curl now, got TIME_TOTAL:0.42 for a 200 earlier, but the failing one that triggered the ticket had TIME_TOTAL:1.85 and returned 401. Uploading trace.txt to diag upload id diag_98766.

alex_supp: Thanks — that's actionable. We'll follow up in this thread once infra confirms whether it was an auth backend hiccup or a token acceptance window. Appreciate the quick repro snippets + diag uploads. :thumbsup:

maria_prod: Thanks all, will keep an eye and will post any further req ids if we see more.
